title: Routing fallback software harmonization & parity audit
creator: Ethan Caldwell
description: Background: Smart routing uses tier and region selection plus variant fallbacks to guarantee SLOs. Recent canary failures showed mismatches in tokenization and KV cache keys between primary and fallback variants, causing truncated generations and incorrect prefix reuse. This ticket is to perform a one-off harmonization audit and then bake the results into an ongoing "parity registry" and CI gates. Scope: (1) inventory encoding/decoder differences across curated model families, (2) validate context-window contracts (max_len, pad behavior, eos handling), (3) confirm tooling invariants (KV layout, cache keying, chunking heuristics), (4) add automated parity checks in variant onboarding and routing path CI, (5) runbook updates for on-call and rollout engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive inventory CSV generated with encoding, max_context, pad and eos semantics for all models in catalog
Automated unit tests added to model-onboarding CI that fail on tokenizer/kv-parity regressions
Runtime sanity check implemented in request router: if hash(context) or tokenizer fingerprint differs between primary and candidate fallback, route to safe fallback or short-circuit
Runbook and incident playbook updated and reviewed by SRE and runtime leads
Two-stage canary rollout plan validated on staging traffic and observed over 48h with no user-impacting regressions
decisions: Adopt a canonical tokenizer fingerprint (sha256 of byte encoder table + normalization rules) stored in the parity registry
Enforce a tolerance policy for context-window incompatibilities: if fallback max_context < primary by more than 128 tokens, avoid automated fallback
Prefer soft-fallback (truncate+notify) over hard-fail for low-importance routes during transitional rollouts
Integrate parity checks into pre-deploy gating rather than runtime-only to catch regressions earlier
implementation_notes: Step 1: Run the inventory script (scripts/parity_audit/generate_inventory.py) across model catalog snapshots; produce CSV and JSONL artifacts
Step 2: Implement tokenizer-fingerprint unit in model registry service (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1456)
Step 3: Add router-side guard that consults registry before allowing fallback; fallback decision tree documented in docs/runbooks/fallback-guard.md
Step 4: Add telemetry metrics: fallback_mismatch_count, fallback_blocked_count, tokenizer_fingerprint_mismatch_rate; hook into Console dashboard
Step 5: Add CI test permalinks and flakiness thresholds; failure must post a blocking comment on PR with remediation hints
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ethan Caldwell: Created ticket after staging canary showed truncated outputs for europen-v1 -> europe-v1-quant fallback. Attached initial CSV snapshot from artifact run.

2025-02-15 - Priya Nair: Completed first-pass inventory. Found three model families where byte-encoder mapping differs due to historical tokenizer normalization change. Raised github PR to add canonical fingerprint generator. Linking PR.
2025-02-18 - Marta Sousa (SRE): Reviewed runtime guard design. Suggested metric names and alert thresholds: alert if tokenizer_fingerprint_mismatch_rate > 0.5% over 5m on prod routes.

2025-02-22 - Design Review (Liam Chen): UX for fallbacks should surface explicit user-visible degrade reason. Decided to add a structured event in streaming responses when a soft-fallback truncation occurs.

2025-02-27 - Priya Nair: Implemented router guard prototype and ran controlled staging rollout (10% traffic). Observed 0.12% blocked fallbacks; investigations show most are benign due to whitespace-normalization differences. Next step: add normalization auto-patch in onboarding to reduce noise.

2025-03-01 - Ethan Caldwell: Scheduling final validation run over 48h in canary. If green, promote PR and schedule runtime-1.20 backport. Noted remaining follow-ups for ops to tune alerts and for legal to review audit logs retention.
incident_learnings: INC-2025-02-tokenization-regression: root cause was silent tokenizer change in upstream model conversion script; mitigation added to onboarding checklist
Postmortem summary: add parity checks to model bundle validator and stop silent in-place tokenizer edits to published artifacts
risk_mitigation: Run staged rollouts with opaque traffic tagging so we can quickly rollback routing policy changes
Keep a pinned fallback for high-value routes (enterprise tenants) that bypasses automated fallback selection until manual sign-off
Set conservative alert thresholds first to avoid alert fatigue; iterate after signal quality improves
